summary.intent: Prepare the caliper alpha: publish docs for the checker default and known limits, measure performance and quality on current main, and diagnose why Storybook Controls show hundreds of rows and why React props vanish from CLI output. The user then pushed back that the full-HTML default contradicts the goal of producing the best results rather than overwhelming numbers.
summary.outcome: Docs PR #489 was pushed. The measurement report was written to REPORT.md, and the 437-row and React-props-recall issues were diagnosed as intended-but-flawed behavior. A T4 worker was started to list props by usage evidence in both lanes, and the terminology sweep (stop calling the checker an add-on) is promised but not yet done.

repo: Both lanes (CLI checker lane and Storybook session lane) disagree on the same options: CLI shows Button with 150 props and Badge with 2, while Storybook shows 437 and 280.
Collapse exempts @types/react props by design, so DOM props never collapse under the addon default htmlAttributes 'full'.
Chakra's 130 Conditions props (_active, 2xl, ...) fall below the 200-prop collapse threshold and are not recognized as ambient by name.

The CLI whole-project merge drops React props whenever an element layer exists (since commit d072b2ed, 0.8.0 to 0.11.0), but that layer carries no member names, so CLI and RDT-format consumers get no DOM prop names.
The weekly oracle runs out of Node heap on Chakra at about 4 GB and needs a 16 GB heap; the rerun finished with 75.5% of Chakra props 'not judged' (Mantine 62.9%), with 0 wrong.
Sandbox blocks git fetch (ssh to github.com) and npm registry access, so subagent worktrees are built on the last fetched origin/main (de016f69) and cannot run pnpm lint; CI runs lint.
The 0.11.0 CI weekly of 2026-11-15 died with exit 143 on the Chakra Caliper step, and 0.11.0 as released needed 42 GB on Chakra.

code.finding: Storybook keeps every @types/react prop under the default htmlAttributes 'full'.
Collapse exempts React types, so DOM props are never collapsed.
CLI merge drops React props when an element layer exists, since d072b2ed.

workflow: Subagent hand-backs are not user approval; the lead verified claims (e.g. diagnosis.md) before acting and asked the user for a go-ahead on a contract change.
A subagent's Write to REPORT.md was refused, so the lead wrote the file from the hand-back text instead.
Using a pushed branch plus gh pr list --head to find the PR number worked after a first gh pr edit with backticks in the body was awkward; a second edit without backticks succeeded.
Timings taken at load average 5 to 10 are inflated, so memory and size figures are more trustworthy than wall times.

friction: Machine load never dropped below 5, so all timings are noisy and a clean re-timing is still needed.
git fetch and the npm registry were blocked in the sandbox, so lint could not run locally and the worktree was based on a possibly stale main.
The subagent's Write of REPORT.md was refused and the classifier was unavailable for a later Edit, requiring a retry.
The Chakra oracle ran out of Node heap on the first attempt, and the Storybook restart was refused, leaving prefetch unmeasured.
antd could not be measured in Storybook because Vite failed on the generated ./version import.
The lead started T4 before answering the user's pushback, and the user's 'add-on' wording intent was ambiguous since the Storybook package is literally an addon.
open_items: Resolve the 0.11.0 release recovery: delete the mismatched asset and re-dispatch, or skip with RELEASE_PENDING_FROM.
Decide the alpha audience and whether the collapseInheritedProps default flip ships in the first alpha.
Finish T4 (list props by usage evidence in both lanes) and reconsider the htmlAttributes 'full' default, since the user wants the best results rather than huge row counts.
Sweep docs, changesets and READMEs to replace 'add-on' wording with 'TypeScript checker (on by default)' and drop optional-sounding opt-out language.
Fix the weekly oracle step: set a larger Node heap for Chakra, and either judge cut types or report 'not judged' separately.
Fix the weekly recall metric or make the CLI merge honor htmlAttributes so React props are not counted as missing.
Consider recognizing Chakra Conditions as an ambient layer (Button drops to about 37 rows).
Investigate why the oracle leaves 63 to 75% of Mantine and Chakra props not judged.
Re-time on an idle machine, then refresh the STATUS.md speed numbers and write the changeset after T4 lands.
Review MIGRATING.md in full and verify the '0.7 to 2.9 s' Chakra Button figure against the oracle run.
Measure prefetch for neighbouring versus distant stories and the warm-restart ready time.
